answer:
HYPOTHESIS: The two cultural-capital diversity indicators first show opposite growth trends in the **18th century BCE (1800–1701 BCE)** — the earliest (and effectively only) century in the 4100–500 BCE record where they diverge. Over that century, **Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased significantly** (Zkeverz from −0.48 to +0.97, Δ = +1.45 z-scores ≈ +0.0145 z/yr) while **Diversity in Pottery Form declined simultaneously** (ZKeform from +0.74 to −1.13, Δ = −1.87 z-scores ≈ −0.0187 z/yr), with Pottery Form falling to its record minimum. Before this century the two series move in lockstep (both rising or both falling), so the 18th c. BCE is the first time the required pattern (Decoration up + Form down) occurs.

The result is robust: it is unchanged across the threshold sweep (θ = 0 pure sign-flip, 0.5, 1.0, and the 90th-percentile magnitude cut ≈ 0.555 of |Δ|), and identical whether using the raw values, the linearly-interpolated values (identical at the centennial anchors) or the independent capital.csv dataset (all cross-checks max abs diff = 0.0000).

Uncertainty note: the indicators are only resolved at 100-year centennial bins that sit exactly on century boundaries, so the same 1800→1700 BCE change could alternatively be attributed to the **17th century BCE (1700–1601 BCE)** under an end-point labeling convention; the direction and magnitude of the divergence are unaffected by this labeling choice. (Context only, not a driver: the divergence coincides with the LN→OBA cultural-phase transition, and regional pollen openness (Belau/Woserin mean PC1) edged down slightly over the same interval, 2.26 → 1.89.)

payload.hypothesis: In the 18th century BCE (1800-1701 BCE) — the first century in the 4100-500 BCE record where the two cultural-capital diversity indicators diverge — Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased significantly (Zkeverz -0.48 -> +0.97, Δ=+1.45 z-scores) while Diversity in Pottery Form declined simultaneously (ZKeform +0.74 -> -1.13, Δ=-1.87 z-scores, a record low). This is the earliest chronological opposite-trend event; before it the two series co-move. Robust across a threshold sweep (θ=0, 0.5, 1.0, and 90th-percentile ≈0.555) and identical for raw, interpolated, and capital.csv values. Alternative label under an end-point convention: 17th century BCE (1700-1601 BCE).
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded all 3 CSVs with correct decimal handling (time_series_data.csv = period; capital.csv and pollen = comma/EU). 2) Verified CE = 1950 - calBP exactly (max abs diff 0.0); cultural record 4100-500 BCE, raw cultural-capital Z-values present only at 37 centennial points. 3) Confirmed raw centennial values == _inter at anchors == capital.csv ZKeform/Zkeverz (max abs diff 0.0000). 4) Derived centuries from CE (oldest->newest) and computed the century-to-century simple difference d (== 100-yr slope) for PotteryDecoration and PotteryForm; used simple difference not % change because values are signed z-scores. 5) Applied (Deco d>0 AND Form d<0, with magnitude threshold) and swept θ = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 90th-pct(≈0.555); earliest qualifying century identical in all cases = 18th c. BCE. 6) Labeled per standard convention (18th c. BCE = 1800-1701 BCE), noting the 17th-c. BCE alternative. 7) Cross-referenced culture phases (LN->OBA) and pollen openness as context only.
